notes: Two university-layer documents (Guidelines for Using Generative AI; OTL Concerns About Student Use), both delegates for both coders. Disagreements on matched units: (1) policy type, 6 units: data-use condition P50 vs P65 (P65, it makes use depend on tool review and contract terms); the two IT-contact lines P72 vs P10 (split: 'If you aren't sure, contact the IT help center' is ask-before-use, P10; 'Work with the IT staff ... explore use cases' is help, P72); 'take the time to have a conversation' P57 vs P68 (P57, no consequence is described); misuse-handling 'you can decide how to proceed' P85/may vs P04/informs (P04, may); Career office AI guide P44 vs P70 (P44, student, during-work, a resource not training). (2) phase, 4 units: syllabus statement and early writing sample (course-start, communicating expectations), career guide, tutorials (before-course). (3) modality, 2 units: disclosure 'should be clearly documented and disclosed' (should, as the source says) and the 'you can decide' line (may). (4) actor, 1 unit (career guide). unit_stance differences (not scored) were resolved by reading the sentence's own position: neutral for compliance and verify rules, permit for 'edit their own work after using AI'. Only-A units, both kept: the 'Protect confidential, copyrighted, and personal information' heading and the 'Any AI tool ... must follow review processes' heading. Only-B units, all kept: the OTL purpose sentence, the 'training data' sentence, the 'copyright-protected or proprietary information' clause, and the Writing Center 'own voices' recommendation. Sample-syllabus P63 unit given a normalized policy limited to the first sentence. No UNCOVERED units and no new types; all fit_notes from both coders were kept or merged.
